title: Number of Rental Property Service Contracts a Landlord May Hold
content:
A landlord may hold any number of Rental Property Service Contracts, one per rental property. There is no maximum number of rental contracts per landlord.

How many contracts one property may carry is governed by the rule that a rental property carries only one service contract at a time, and how the landlord's contracts combine for pricing is governed by the portfolio discount terms.

| Question the rule answers | Answer |
|---|---|
| Is there a cap on the number of rental contracts one landlord holds? | No cap. |
| What does one contract cover? | One rental property. |
| Can one landlord hold contracts on several properties at once? | Yes, one contract for each property. |

*Hypothetical illustration:* a landlord who owns twelve rented houses may hold twelve Rental Property Service Contracts, one on each house.
